events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. The trace settles the timing element: the rider cancelled 175 s (2 min 55 s) after matching, i.e. within 3 minutes [F2], so the NS-4 free-cancellation branch applies and the $6.61 fee is not chargeable [F5][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show route cannot support the fee either. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was logged [F4], and the driver was never within 200 m of the pickup (closest approach 2189 m at the moment of cancellation) [F1][F3]. NS-1 (i) and (ii) therefore fail, and under NS-2 the $6.61 must be returned in full [NS-1][NS-2]. The driver's own written statement, made after the trip, only says he was "on my way" [F10], which is consistent with the GPS record [F1] and does not create any fee entitlement.

The driver's 14:06 chat message giving "5 min more" [F8] confirms he was still far from the pickup about one minute before the cancellation [F2][F1], so the >3 continuous minutes of waiting at the pickup that NS-1 (iii) requires could not have occurred [NS-1]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9], so this is not a G12 referral situation and the record settles every element above.

No traffic excuse is available or needed: the speed band on Stevens Road (30–39 km/h) and the absence of incidents and rain, in fair weather [F11][F12][F13], satisfy neither RD-4(a) nor RD-4(b), and in any event the fee issue is governed by NS-4 [RD-4].

Amount: the only money in issue is the single cancellation fee of $6.61 with a 1.0× multiplier and no surge [F5][F6]; no trip was performed. The refund is the whole $6.61 [F2][F5][NS-4][NS-7], payable as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.

On the safety screen, I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement: they concern arrival time and the cancellation fee only, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10]. Nothing in the record suggests an account-level abuse of the arrival/cancellation button: no "I'm Here" tap and no fabricated arrival exist [F3][F4][F5], so NS-2's flag_account limb is not triggered.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no account action against the driver.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled at 14:07:55, only 2 min 55 s after matching at 14:05:00, which is within the 3-minute window in which a rider cancellation is not chargeable, so the $6.61 cancellation fee should not have been charged at all.

The driver never arrived: GPS puts his closest approach to the pickup point at 2189 m at the very moment of cancellation, he never came within 200 m, and the timeline records no platform arrival (driver_arrived_at null).

No arrival confirmation exists on record — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was logged (driver_pressed_here_at null) — so the no-show cancellation prerequisites in NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail and the fee must be fully refunded under NS-2.

The driver's written statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" (F10) concedes he had not arrived; it also conflicts with the GPS record that he was still 2189 m away, and the system record wins over his statement.

The driver's own chat message at 14:06 told the rider he needed "5 min more", so at the 14:07:55 cancellation he was still roughly 4 minutes from arriving; this corroborates the GPS that he could not have been waiting at the pickup point for the 3 continuous minutes NS-1 (iii) requires.
The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F9), so there is no evidentiary gap that would force this no-show dispute to be referred to a human instead of decided.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window and the road speed band on Stevens Road was 30–39 km/h in fair weather with no rain, so slow traffic cannot justify the driver's failure to reach the pickup point.

Although $6.61 is the published cancellation fee amount, no cancellation-fee event was established because the driver neither arrived nor tapped "I'm Here", so the fee must be returned in full to the rider (Ryde voucher form per policy).

weaknesses: The rider cancelled after matching rather than waiting, and the rider has an existing dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14), so the judge may view the cancellation as avoidable — though NS-4 fixes the fee question purely on the 3-minute clock (F2).

The driver's profile is clean and long-standing: 4.0 years, rating 4.77, 652 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes (F15), which may invite sympathy for his "I was on my way" statement (F10) even though the GPS contradicts it (F1).

The driver did message proactively at 14:06 giving an ETA of 5 more minutes (F8); the other side may argue the rider knew a short wait was needed, but NT/NS provide no obligation on the rider to keep waiting, and Ryde has no published free-cancellation rule for a late driver (NS-8 is informational and cannot be applied).

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled only 2 min 55 s after matching (accepted 14:05:00, rider cancellation 14:07:55), i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

No-show branch (RD/NS-1) never opens against the driver here: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped “I’m Here” and no automatic arrival was recorded (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the NS-1 (i)-(ii) prerequisites for retaining the fee are not met.

The system GPS record confirms the rider's account of the facts rather than contradicting it: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2189 m at 14:07:55 and he never came within 200 m, consistent with cancellation occurring while the driver was still en route — and that record is not a basis to keep the fee.

The driver's own chat message at 14:06 (“5 min more, traffic is slow”) is a time estimate only, and the driver's post-trip statement “I was on my way when the rider cancelled” concedes he had not reached the pickup point; neither assertion is a claim of rider no-show and neither satisfies NS-1.

The driver did not fabricate a no-show: there is no arrival confirmation of any kind on record to support a $6.61 fee, and the platform's own timeline (no arrival, no “I’m Here” tap) shows the fee was levied automatically on rider cancellation rather than on any driver claim, so no NS-2 abuse finding or account flag is warranted.

The cancellation fee is the only money in issue: the fare record shows the single $6.61 cancellation fee and a 1.0× multiplier with no surge, and no trip was performed, so refunding $6.61 fully resolves the dispute.

The driver's record weighs against any sanction: 1460 days on the platform, rating 4.77, 652 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so the NS-7 remedy (a $6.61 voucher to the rider) disposes of the case without any account action against the driver.

weaknesses: The driver's own message at 14:06 (“5 min more, traffic is slow”, F8) concedes he was still about five minutes away roughly one minute before the rider cancelled, and the GPS record (F1) puts him 2189 m out — the rider will use these to press that the fee was pure windfall; they do not, however, defeat the NS-4 timing defence, which is the point on which the fee actually turns.

The driver never tapped “I’m Here” and no platform arrival was recorded (F3, F4), so the driver has no NS-1 (i)/(ii) basis on which to claim any fee at all (NS-1, NS-2) — the honest position is that the fee should be refunded and the driver does not oppose that refund.

Traffic evidence is at best neutral: F11 shows only 30–39 km/h on Stevens Road during 14:00–14:12 and F12 records no incidents, with fair weather (F13); under RD-4(c) this cannot be dressed up as a “reasonable cause” that justifies delay, and it is not offered as a defence to the fee.

The rider's profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F14) — thin ammunition, but the rider may argue a pattern of fee complaints; the driver should not over-rely on it since profile facts cannot decide the case.

points.response: Accepted, and it matches my C1: F2 shows the rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching, inside NS-4's 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 in F5 is not chargeable.
Accepted: F3 (driver_arrived_at null) and F4 (no "I'm Here" tap, no automatic arrival) mean NS-1 (i)-(ii) are unmet, which is exactly what my C3 asks the judge to find under NS-2.
Accepted — F1 (closest approach 2189 m at 14:07:55, never within 200 m) is a system record that beats any statement, and my C2/C4 rely on it; there is nothing in F1 that supports keeping the fee.
Accepted: F8 and F10 admit the driver had not reached the pickup point (F10 says only "on my way"), so no NS-1 claim survives; I note only that F10 also conflicts with F1 and cannot help the driver.
Accepted that F3/F4/F5 show no fabricated arrival, so I do not press a flag_account; my C8 rests on NS-2 full refund, not on abuse.
Accepted: F5 (single $6.61 cancellation fee) and F6 (1.0× multiplier, no surge, no trip performed) mean a full $6.61 refund closes the case under NS-7.
Accepted as far as it goes: F15 shows a clean driver record, so no account action is sought; F14 likewise supports no flag against the rider, and NS-7 voucher form remains the remedy.

Conceded — the driver does not contest this: the rider cancelled at 14:07:55, 2 min 55 s after matching at 14:05:00 (F2), which is within the 3-minute window in NS-4, so the $6.61 fee recorded at F5 is not chargeable to the rider.

The driver accepts this record; it is the same GPS timeline in my brief (F1, F3) and is precisely why the driver does not resist the refund — the driver was 2189 m away and never within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails and the fee cannot be kept.
Conceded as to the outcome: no “I’m Here” tap and no automatic arrival are on record (F4), so NS-1 (i) fails, the fee is refundable and the driver's own brief already asks for exactly that.

The driver does not dispute that the system record beats his statement: the GPS closest approach of 2189 m at 14:07:55 (F1) and the null arrival field (F3) control over the post-trip wording at F10, and the statement was only ever an explanation that he was still en route, not a no-show claim.

This corroboration runs the driver's way on the fee: with a 14:06 “5 min more” estimate (F8), the driver could not have been stationary inside 200 m for the >3 continuous minutes NS-1 (iii) requires before the 14:07:55 cancellation (F2), so no no-show fee event exists.

The driver agrees the chatbot record is complete and timestamped (F9), so no G12 referral is needed and this dispute can be decided on the records — a refund_full of the $6.61 on the face of NS-4, not an escalation.

The driver does not offer traffic as a defence to the fee: F11 (30–39 km/h band on Stevens Road), F12 (no incidents) and F13 (fair, 0 mm) cannot satisfy RD-4(a), and RD-4(b) alone does not exempt, so the driver's late arrival is simply not excused — and equally not a basis to charge the rider.

Agreed on the remedy: with no arrival event (F4, F1) the $6.61 at F5 is unsupported, and under NS-7 it should be returned to the rider as a Ryde voucher — which is the driver's own requested outcome, so the rider's ask and the driver's brief coincide.
